newsitem.title: GERMANY: German utility IAW says H1 96/97 earnings rise.
newsitem.headline: German utility IAW says H1 96/97 earnings rise.

text.p: German utility Isar-Amperwerke AG (IAW) said on Saturday that earnings in the first half of its 1996/97 business year increased, despite a fall-off in sales over the period.

Net profit at the Bavarian power company, currently a takeover target for German mixed utility Viag AG increased to 55 million marks in the six months to the end of December 1996, from 44 million a year previously.
IAW reiterated its outlook given at its annual shareholder meeting at the end of January, forecasting an increase in operating profit in the full year despite a fall in sales because of price cuts.
The group said net profit grew because of a good year in its nuclear energy division, as well as the impact of its cost-cutting programme and a reduction in write-offs.

The group's financial result for the full year would come out around the previous year's level at 127 million marks, while profit from ordinary activities would exceed the previous year's figure of 225 million marks.
Meanwhile sales fell 1.6 percent to 976 million marks after IAW introduced price cuts for special contract customers.
Net electricity sales increased by 0.4 percent to 5.32 billion kilowatt hours.
IAW's investments in the period were 171 million marks, up from 167 million a year earlier, and IAW said the investments would reach 325 million in the full year.
The number of employees at the group fell by 3.8 percent to 2,880 as part of the group's restructuring plan.
Since May last year, Viag has been trying, through its Bavarian utility Bayernwerk, to secure a majority stake in IAW and a decision is still awaited from the German cartel office.
